text:
Alyssa: quick heads-up — during today's perf run i saw a ~25% TPS drop on prefill-heavy traffic when we enable per-op calibration for int8 on long-context jobs (64k). TTFT for cold requests jumps. perf-bot posted traces.
Mike: repro steps? which model/config and what was the load pattern?
Alyssa: repro: redwood/gptx-3b-quant, ctx=65536, quant=calibrated-int8 (calib enabled per-op), microbatch=8, single-request prefill-heavy (client sends large prompt then short decode). Observed prefill lat median 420ms -> 780ms with calib on. Overall TPS down ~25%.
Raj: can you drop the profile stdout? my hunch is kernel selection flipping mid-prefill causing dequant/quantize thrash + KV churn.
Alyssa: pasted snippet from perf-bot (flamegraph + short summary):

perf-bot: https://perf.internal/runs/1748654321
perf-bot: summary: prefill time increased 86ms per layer on average for layers 20-26; kernel switch detected from `fp8_fused_attn_v2` -> `int8_dequant_path_v1` during prefill; KV eviction went up 3x resulting in extra prefill passes.

Mike: that kernel switch is suspicious. did the kernel selector fallback because calibration altered the scale params? any quant table mismatches? 
Raj: profiler shows calibration path adds an `emit_calib` pass before matmul which disables fused fp8 kernel for those layers. Combined with our batching heuristic that treats long-prefill requests as low-latency targets (TTFT-first), requests avoid being coalesced — so we lose TPS and hit repeated prefill work.
Sasha: two things to try: 1) make batching heuristic prefer grouping prefill phases when ctx>32k (temporarily bump `prefill_group_window_ms`), 2) pin kernel_selector to `force_fp8_fused_attn` for A/B to confirm impact. Also consider making calibration a background async job rather than inline per-request for long contexts.
Alyssa: I'm running an A/B now: calib on + force fp8 fused vs calib on + default selector. will post numbers. quick config I used:
```
kernel_selector: auto
quant_mode: calibrated-int8
batching:
  microbatch_size: 8
  prefill_group_window_ms: 4
kv:
  eviction_policy: lru
  max_tokens: 200000
```
Mike: if we confirm it's the inline calibration path causing kernel disable, we should change the calibration orchestration: do it once at model load or as a low-priority async step that updates runtime flags without forcing per-request kernel downgrades.
Raj: also check KV cache pinning. profiler shows many small evictions around layer boundaries when kernel toggles — that indicates our KV layout vs kernel memory layout mismatch. pinning KV for fused kernels reduced eviction count in a quick local run.
Alyssa: thanks — will share the A/B numbers shortly. if anyone wants to help triage: please grep the perf trace for `kernel-switch` and `kv-evict` events; I left the lightweight trace at perf-bot link.
perf-bot: attached trace artifacts: flamegraph, layer-level latencies, kernel-selection timeline (see link above).
